When he was found, he did 12 not say to the Blessed Virgin that he stopped to please himself; no, he said that he stopped because it was the will of his Father, who for this sent him on earth. ||

Will and Love. 4th Conference

In my dear Crucifix, my dear daughters, allow me to tell you how through our will we embitter the heart of Jesus.

Tell me, do you think that because you are superiors it is right for you to do your own will? Why this? It is immediately explained; you do not love at all.

13 The person who loves has no will, but only tries to seek the will of God who well taught us to submit our || will to that one of God.

Well, let us see if we can put this into practice.

Circular letters are sent repeatedly, inculcating the love of the sisters who depend on you and to care that they may miss nothing. If they have a small sickness, cure them, submitting yourselves to be their nurses.

Oh – it is said – she has nothing! She has a strong headache but she has no fever; she need not to go to bed!

My God, do you love Jesus? No, because one who loves God is all heart || for her neighbour. 14 These are not my inventions, but every morning we promise to love our neighbour for his love and for this we will give a strict account.

There are certain others full of care; to appear nicely, they do all they can so that their houses may be well in order. The confessor comes and what is done; the president…so that nothing may be lacking.

Let us look at the maintenance of the sisters: how they are dressed, the shoes they wear, if… || Horror! They lack everything. 15 Perhaps there might be one who misses nothing, the one who is always close to her.

Food is never eaten in the dining room and if it is done, it is for the sake of appearance. Maybe the sisters should believe the superior lives by the Holy Spirit. The poor see that these do not eat, they are ashamed. But soon Jesus helps them to discover and then one passes the voice to another: “Last evening the superior together… It was eleven o’clock and they were eating…”

16 Curiosity led them to go early || to see if they could get something. There was a chicken bone. If you superior want to eat chicken, why not cook it for all three and you could eat even an entire one. The person who follows the Saviour does not seek to satisfy greed but works with Jesus seeking to do the will of God. ||

17 Will and Love. 5th Conference

It seems that Jesus says: “I came poor into the world without a cradle, without a house; I wept from cold and two animals warmed me, the charity of the good shepherds brought me what was necessary and I thanked them with a smile.”

My dear Love, who induced you to bear so much suffering?

The will of my Father to free thankless human beings from slavery.

Oh, so much love! Well, do you believe it? 18 When houses are opened || if they are beautiful and well repaired it is all right. Otherwise they say: “Oh, what horror! Before they accept such a house it would be important to send someone to visit it. What a bad place!”

Will and Love. 6th Conference

How is it that Jesus has suffered poverty for human beings and we do not do anything; neither deprivation nor other things. We want everything beautiful and right, according to our 19 desire. There is little love for work and especially coldness in the spirit that should be all on fire for the Institute. ||

Will and love. 7th Conference

Here we are at the end of our Spiritual Exercises. Alas!

I give a look and see I did not profit at all. But certainly I do not want to believe it is the same for you.

I hope that you are all full of fervour, all with firm commitments written and sealed in your hearts so that you may never fail.

20 “Jesus, sweetest, how quickly we reached Tabor and we were comfortable, || but how much you suffered to reach here! No, dear Saviour, if humanity would stop the spirit is ready to follow you everywhere, until Calvary. I know well that only this mountain sealed your love.”

Let us try to be used to think well of all and love all especially those who cause us pain and troubles.

To love those who do good to us and who love us is something that comes by itself and for nothing…one does it even with pleasure.

6. CONFERENCES TO THE SUPERIORS OF SICILY

FROM 1ST MARCH TO 9 MAY 1898

1 MS 10. 6 – pp. 1 - 25

MEMOIRS OF 1898

1st March: left Rome. Today 2nd day, in Naples: a bit of work and arrangement of the sisters.

9 March: Arrival in Palermo in via d’Ossuna.

12 April 1898: Spiritual Exercises. 1st Conference: charity.

The person who possesses this treasure is sure of receiving many graces from the Lord. Charity conceals our imperfections and covers our miseries before the spouse; the deformities of our actions are embellished by it. 2 Who would not wish to possess such a treasure that covers us with a heavenly mantle || and this is studded with precious pearls according to the degree of charity we possess!

One day a charitable person received many insults and accusations from the one whom she/he benefited. She/he lamented with the Lord because she/he was treated that way. Perhaps that charity was not done well or was not done with the right intention. Here is the answer she/he got: “For charity to bring real advantage to the person who does it should be made perfect in this way; it is not perfect unless it goes through this way of being molested.”

3 She is a thankless sister - || said a superior – I do not want to do anything. Let her bust by the work, but I will not relieve her. It seems that all should be obliged to her! Instead of a “thank you” she turns her shoulders or grumbles; is this gratitude?

Pity! How much this creature has lost! With a “thank you” she was paid, but Jesus does not act like this. Charity to be perfect should not expect gratitude; it is better a sign in the big book rather than a “thank you” and attention of acknowledgement on this earth of pains and worries. ||

Continues.

2. 4 Ge… The attachment we should have to the dear

Institute.

Isn’t reproaching a sister a failure in charity; it is said:

“You are rude, an orphan, you were ragged!”

When Peter betrayed him our Lord said: “Why did you betray me?” Peter wept and he was forgiven. He did not say: “You were a poor rough fisherman” and other words, no. Who was Paul whom the Lord made an apostle and infused in him much wisdom? To whom did the Blessed

Virgin always appear? To farmers. ||

5 And the poor cook, how many things they go through!

They are humiliated! Never admitted to recreation! The worst is one or more superiors used to slap them; what a pain for us!

Poor creatures, they would merit a thousand regards! It is odd if they have a sister who dares to answer… Certainly the cook is much oppressed and if she is overcome by anger she answers; then it is done. It is said that she must be transferred, that what we have done is nothing and a superior is put to the test… They even put the poor cook to sleep in garret, without either a door or || a window. What cold she can get! 6 I appeal to you dear daughters; what did this merit?

Another one slapped her; and I would much prefer to say, but with only one word you can understand everything.

//

7 2nd Conference on the attachment we should have to the dear Institute. Not as certain say as when they write to me:

“Your Institute,” horror! It has never been mine, I had nothing and I might have done only evil to it, but certainly not purposely. I only know of being a true ass of the Lord, because in order to make his work shine more he made me love him so much to a point that I preferred him to my own life; but the Institute should never be called mine.

I do not know why certain sisters have little love for it; 8 and it is true what || the administrations do, little interested as they are for its growth; they care for nothing but only for their houses. They want sisters; they want many things and never care for the interest of the Institute. How much pain I feel! 9 Something will be said on the growth of the same and also how the Lord helps us in this time. ||

10 11 3rd Conference

How the superiors should be watchful and think that all the actions of the sisters depend on them in every community. The superior must be docile, kindly, and very watchful over the sisters so that they may not commit things against the Rule and so that the time-table may be followed properly.

She should be prompt for meditation and all the sisters in that house exemplary. All will grow old attending to their duties and die holy. If the head is holy the parts are also holy; but for certain superiors this speech is annoying.

[Blank page]

4th Conference

Dear daughters, today I desire many things from you; that every one who is questioned answers frankly and speaks her opinion frankly, sincere as the heart dictates to her without fear of being mistaken; as an affectionate daughter to her mother who tells what her heart dictates to her.

When it is ordered by the major superiors to transfer a superior who is in danger because of the lay persons or priests, what would you do?

When the transfer is ordered she rebels 12 speaking slanders, what should be done?

When it is certain || that she sends money or other things to her family or makes big gifts which our poverty does not allow, what should be done?

Should a rule be established for all regarding baths? I say my opinion, what do you say?

To the Congregation of Bishops and Regulars is said that one dress is kept…

Tell me, what meaning or rather what horrible impression does it make when we hear that in a city in which there are many houses a superior back-bites much with those in the other houses; it is only she who does well!

What a pain! ||

13 Take care of the conscience because what one accuses the other one and uses the other sister to increase… not all is true. For pity’s sake I appeal to your criterion: what should be done?

Is it right to remove the main dish from the sisters in order to make gifts with that money? ||

14 5th Conference

Our treatment today will be pleasing to all. We will give much news about the growth of the Institute and as it was announced in the circular letter of invitation, we will speak about the good work that God is pleased to do pouring his graces and treasures to his dear Institute.

All the news is given… ||

15 6th Conference

The person who loves does not hurt the beloved but tries all she/he can to relieve her/him. Therefore?

We have said that the weaknesses of the sisters should never be made known to anybody and a superior should hide them as much as she can from the others. When you are requested, if you have a sister for abroad, if you have a good subject you say no. In this way we never have one for a superior. Why? 16 I have only one superior who is really good and fully for the Institute; she forms the sisters || and then she informs me: “I have one, and I think she will do well.”

17 This is what really happens, but she is the only one because the others when they have good ones, they never want them to be transferred; in this, there is failure in the love one should have for the Institute. ||

7th Conference

Dear daughters, your affection towards me fills me with strength to support the sweet burden that Jesus placed on my breast. I will never put on my shoulders the dear and beloved cross, no. Therefore, with much simplicity, those who have desire to know something… ||

18 April

For the Spiritual Exercises of the sisters.

For the construction that Father Federico did. It seems to me odd that we should suffer more for a stranger than for the good of the Institute.

I must recommend again that you should keep the sick sisters. There is a recent event: the poor superior suffered because the president of the blind no longer wanted the cook who was sick who had worked much for that house. Well, what did I do? 19 Florio came to see me and I recommended her; || I had even written earlier.

She then gave an order that the sister should not be touched and provided an armchair so that the sister who had heart sickness could use it; but for the sisters it was a bit demanding, is it true? If all the superiors could do the same! I recommend … It is true that there are twenty-nine in G.(Gargatano) but those who are really sick may reach ten; the others have the head on…

20 For the store-house they should use Rome. ||

7 C… 1898

For the name-day.

For going out with the apron and the small veil.

Not to leave money for the sisters which can be spent, like selling books…

In the visits in the towns do not receive the administrators except with much precaution etc.

Love much the honour of the Institute.

21 Have many precautions in keeping girls and women of service. ||

Speak about the abuse of wine; in the same way after 31 years of vocation they suspect that one can commit the sin of…

Listen to all, do not do as the last time in the Chapter;

those accusations that they made were truly curious; they made me laugh, especially that…

Do you know the word I forgot yesterday? If I could have done that I would end up in censure. Oh, really beautiful! To wait to become old in order to commit such sins! And in these times in which I have a thousand eyes and bonds upon me… ||

22 Do you know the least I could do? 60,000 £…

The same is for many other times. Don’t you think that I fear, no, no; if they give, it is their duty!

The silk handkerchief even one, pale red; the shoes with high heels that have been observed by the priests and lay, the mark of the stuff; the panties a bit tight and close-fitting and with lace; bed-cover and clothes.

People are welcomed in bed room and someone must have become godmother in Baptism or Confirmation.

23 To say that I answered that letter and in this way I said || what a handling was there. Stuff that belongs to the Lord and which has never belonged to me. This wound is deadly; but I forgive. I only speak of what belongs to me […]; I want to do what I want.

They are transferred from one house and they carry away everything; they put in pocket the surplus and they do not think that it is not their stuff but belongs to the Institute.

Others give the stuff to be kept for them. Horror! ||

24 The person who loves does not require much instruction.
